chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja‘far ibn Bashir, from Isma‘il ibn Muhammad al-Khuza‘i, who said:
Abu Basir asked Aba ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام while I was listening, and he said: “Do you think I will reach al-Qa’im عليه السلام?”
He said: “O Abu Basir, do you not know your Imam?” He said: “Yes, by Allah, and you are he,” and he took his hand.
So he said: “By Allah, O Abu Basir, it will not matter to you if you are not sitting with your sword in the shade of the portico of al-Qa’im, may the blessings of Allah be upon him.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, addressed by his kunyah
key_terms.أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: Abu Basir, the questioner in this hadith
key_terms.إِمَامَكَ: your Imam, the divinely designated leader whom one must recognize
key_terms.الْقَائِمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: the awaited Qa’im عليه السلام from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.تَعْرِفُ: to know or recognize with true awareness
key_terms.مُحْتَبِيًا: sitting with one’s limbs gathered, in a prepared or settled posture

ai.seo_question: If a believer recognizes his Imam, does it matter whether he lives to see al-Qa’im عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that recognizing one’s Imam is the essential matter, such that the delay or arrival of the rise of al-Qa’im عليه السلام does not harm the believer who has true ma‘rifah. It emphasizes the theological importance of Imamate and indicates that knowing the present Imam carries the spiritual value of witnessing the awaited Qa’im’s era.
